title: Null homotopy for ordered restriction kernel
statement: Let X be a scheme, I a linearly ordered type, U : I -> Opens(X) any family, F a presheaf of abelian groups, and S chosen finite products over the terminal open with their universal properties [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. Let f be an endomorphism of S.complex(F). Suppose for every degree p, cochain s and strictly increasing tuple t, the t-coordinate of f_p(s) is zero. Then f is homotopic to zero.

source.place: Tag 01FM, equations 20.23.6.1 and 20.23.6.2; precompose the composite contraction with f

proof.text: Use the explicit finite-sum H operator and the first identity to obtain a canonical null homotopy with p-th map id-kappa.
Use the explicit finite-sum K operator and the second identity to obtain a canonical null homotopy with p-th map kappa-P.

Add these null homotopies. In every degree the kappa terms cancel, yielding id-P. For every t and every permutation sigma in the strictly-increasing filter, hf says that (f_p(s))(t composed sigma)=0; transport, integer scalar multiplication, and the finite sum preserve zero. Hence f_p followed by P_p is zero. Precompose the sum homotopy by f; its underlying chain map equals f degreewise. The zero target remains zero under precomposition.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01FM, equations 20.23.6.1 and 20.23.6.2; explicit finite-sum operators and Lean composition

lean.statement:
theorem alternatingCechKernelNullHomotopic (X : Scheme.{u}) {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I]
    (U : I → X.Opens) (F : X.Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w})
    (S : SiteCechComplex U (fun i ↦ homOfLE (le_top : U i ≤ ⊤)))
    (f : S.complex F ⟶ S.complex F)
    (hf : ∀ (p : ℕ) (s : S.cochains F p)
      (t : {t : Fin (p + 1) → I // StrictMono t}), (f.f p s) t.1 = 0) :
    Nonempty (Homotopy f 0)
